name: Abū Zayd Saʿīd ibn Aws al-Anṣārī
summary: Basran lexicographer, trusted above all for what he heard from the Arabs; his al-Nawādir is one of the oldest books of the language, and Sībawayh is said to mean him when he cites 'one I trust'.
bio: Abū Zayd belonged to the Khazraj of Medina by descent and lived in Basra, where he learnt from Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ and collected the speech of the Bedouin. Al-Zubaydī places him in the third generation of the Basran lexicographers. Of the three great lexicographers of his age, al-Aṣmaʿī, Abū ʿUbayda and Abū Zayd, the sources call him the most trustworthy, and Sībawayh's 'I was told by one I trust' is said to refer to him.
His Kitāb al-Nawādir, rare words and usages with the verses that attest them, survives, with books on hamza and on rain. He died in Basra in 215/830, said to be over ninety.
